thread.title: Stocks Lower As Big Banks Weigh On Dow, But Apple Bucks Decline

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Stocks Lower As Big Banks Weigh On Dow, But Apple Bucks Decline
text:
Key stock market index funds remained underwater Friday afternoon as JPMorgan ( JPM ) and other bank stocks continued to weigh.
X SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) fell 0.4%, PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) slipped 0.2% and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) edged 0.1% lower in the stock market today . Emerging markets fared worse as iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ( EEM )tumbled 0.9%.
Banks, retail and telecom led the downside among sector funds. SPDR S&P Bank ( KBE ) was down 1.1%. Component stock JPMorgan gave up an early gain to slide nearly 3% despite reporting quarterly results that topped views. The Dow stock fell back below the 200-day line as it works on the right side of a potential base.
Also on the Dow, Goldman Sachs ( GS ) gave up 1.1%. Blue chip techs retreated too, except for Apple ( AAPL ), which rose 0.4%. The iPhone maker continues to pad gains above its 50-day line as it works on a potential flat base.
Gold miners, energy and utilities advanced. VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ( GDX ) and VanEck Vectors Junior Gold Miners ( GDXJ ) each rose nearly 2%. Both ETFs regained their 50-day lines while building cup bases. SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) and iShares Gold Trust ( IAU ) were up about 0.7% each as gold futures climbed.
Bitcoin added 2% to $8,100.64, according to CoinDesk , after opening below the $8,000 level. The digital money rose despite news that $3 million was stolen from Coinsecure, an Indian cryptocurrency exchange. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) popped 7%, on track to extend its win streak to five.
Top Tech Play Apple, Intel ( INTC ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and other top tech stocks came under pressure in recent weeks, but appear to be finding their footing. As such, many tech-focused funds are on the rise.
First Trust Nasdaq 100 Technology Sector Index Fund ( QTEC ) is one of those. The $2.4 billion fund, which marks its 12th anniversary next week, retook its 50-day moving average on Thursday. A convincing move above the line could set up a potential buy opportunity. QTEC was last featured in this ETF column on March 5, as it rebounded off the 50-day line en route to an 11% gain.
The ETF provides equal-weight exposure to technology stocks on the Nasdaq 100 index. Semiconductors accounted for the biggest sector weight as of April 11, at 41% of assets. Software followed at about 34%, internet 11% and computer hardware 8%. Computer services and telecommunications equipment made up less than 3% each.
Top 10 holdings included Intel (which led the Dow Thursday in percentage gains), Adobe Systems ( ADBE ), Microsoft, Apple and chip gear maker ASML Holding ( ASML ). Intel closed at its highest level in more than 17 years Thursday. Apple is holding above its 50-day line, where it has seen resistance, and could form a flat base with a potential 183.60 buy point.
Beating the S&P 500 QTEC gained 5.8% year-to-date through Wednesday, according to Morningstar Inc., vs. the S&P 500's 0.6% deficit. Average annual returns of 20.9%, 23.2% and 15.9% over the past three, five and 10 years, respectively, outpace the S&P 500's 10.2%, 13% and 9.3% gains over those same periods. The ETF bears a 0.60% expense ratio.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Though trade-war and regulatory-scrutiny concerns hurt techs recently, Richard Turnill, BlackRock's global chief investment strategist, remains bullish on the sector.
"We believe recent weakness reflects rising risks but is not a tech wreck in the making," he wrote in a recent report. "Strong fundamentals underpin our preference for the sector."
And techs may get a sales boost, he says.
"The tech sector was a laggard in the binge of earnings upgrades following the U.S. tax overhaul, as it had one of the lowest effective tax rates," he wrote. "But an indirect benefit may be in the offing: Our text analysis of corporate conference calls suggests companies across industries are looking to deploy their tax windfalls on tech spend."
